card.name: Reciprocal drug interaction statements
card.fires_on: Words in the second half of a two-way statement, such as 'vice' in 'vice versa' or the verb after 'does not' when the roles of two drugs are swapped (A does not affect B, B does not affect A).

modes.label: Vice versa
modes.description: The word 'vice' right before 'versa' after a statement about one item acting on another.
modes.example: trandolapril nor<< vice>> versa. Rarely, the dose-independent

modes.label: Reversed-role verb
modes.description: A verb such as affect, alter, cause or changes, placed after a negation or reciprocal phrase, where the second drug is acting on the first.
modes.example: Verapamil does not<< affect>> the pharmacokinetics of propranol

card.writes: Weak output effect; it may favor words that express the other party or the opposite side, such as 'one side' and 'the other party'.
card.plain: It fires when a text says one drug does something to another and then turns it around, saying the reverse also holds.
